comparison: Both evaluate claims C31-C35 about SLC4A expression in human airways. OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED by PCR and RNA-seq with appropriate replication. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether arguments to exclude SLC4A5/SLC4A8 are sufficient, how relative mRNA abundance was determined, and whether bands were confirmed by digestion.

Both evaluate claims C36-C40 about S0859-sensitive currents in human cells. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED despite acknowledging S0859 specificity concerns. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the very small magnitude of S0859-inhibitable current (~1 vs ~20 uAmp/cm2 in similar models) and questioning S0859 selectivity for SLC4A4 versus other SLC4A family members.

Both evaluate claims C41-C46 about intracellular pH measurements in human cells. Both find the data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted the Na+-dependent, bicarbonate-dependent, and S0859-sensitive pH recovery as evidence for SLC4A4 function, with only minor clarification requests about timescale differences.

Both evaluate claims C47-C51 about ASL pH measurements. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with adequate sample size and quantitative data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification about time points for pH settling, the ~2hr timescale difference versus intracellular effects, and confusing significance value presentation.

Both evaluate claims C52-C53, C95 about SLC4A4 localization in human airways. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED showing basolateral membrane staining in ciliated cells. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether SLC4A4 might also be expressed in Club cells (as in mouse) and whether Club cells rather than ciliated cells are the major bicarbonate source, requesting immunostaining in CC10+ cells.

OpenEval evaluates only claims C54-C55 about mouse isoform expression and finds SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers evaluate C54-C64 (broader set including Ussing chamber data) and rate UNCERTAIN, questioning why forskolin/cAMP-induced current is not reduced in bicarbonate-free buffer and how S0859 inhibits 'basal' current after CaCC blockade.

OpenEval evaluates claims C56-C64 about mouse Ussing chamber experiments and finds SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers (evaluating overlapping claims C54-C64) rate UNCERTAIN, raising multiple mechanistic questions about forskolin effects, the role of CaCCs, apical bicarbonate exit pathways, and unexplained transient negative Isc changes.

Both evaluate claims C65-C70 about mouse intracellular pH measurements. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate controls for bicarbonate-dependence, chloride-dependence, and reversibility. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting that some effects are not fully reversible (Figure S3G) and questioning whether this indicates off-target effects or incomplete inhibition.

OpenEval evaluates claims C71-C75, C106 about histology and cellular localization in mouse. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping claims C71-C80 (including additional mucus/epithelial damage claims). Both find SUPPORTED. The differential localization in mouse (Club cells) versus human (ciliated cells) was accepted as an important species difference.

OpenEval evaluates claims C76-C80 about mucus accumulation and epithelial damage in knockout mice and finds SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers evaluate these claims together with C71-C75 and find SUPPORTED, accepting the histological characterization of the phenotype without specific concerns.

Both evaluate claims C81-C84 about intracellular pH in knockout versus wild-type mouse cells. Both find SUPPORTED. The reduced acidification in Slc4a4-/- cells and differential response after UTP washout were accepted as evidence for SLC4A4-dependent bicarbonate accumulation and secretion.

Both evaluate claims C85-C89 about mucociliary clearance in knockout mice. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers noted that direct ASL volume and pH measurements in knockout mice would strengthen the thesis but acknowledged technical challenges, accepting the clearance data as presented.

OpenEval evaluates main conclusions C8-C16 and finds SUPPORTED by convergence of evidence. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping claims C13-C16, C116, C123 and rate UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about confounding factors from systemic metabolic acidosis, whether reduced plasma HCO3- contributes to the phenotype, and whether Isc measurements represent true resting conditions.

Both evaluate claims C92-C93 about species differences in Ca2+ versus cAMP responses. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as an important documented species difference. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning why forskolin/cAMP-induced current is not reduced in bicarbonate-free buffer given that most is CaCC-mediated in mouse trachea.

Both evaluate claim C118 comparing Slc4a4-/- and Slc12a2-/- phenotypes. Both find SUPPORTED. The contrast showing mucus accumulation in Slc4a4-/- but not Slc12a2-/- mice was accepted as evidence that bicarbonate transport is more critical than chloride transport for preventing muco-obstruction.

OpenEval evaluates C116-C118 about comparative phenotypes and finds SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers evaluate C116 (among other claims) in context of concerns about systemic confounders, rating UNCERTAIN and questioning whether metabolic acidosis contributes to the airway phenotype.

Both evaluate claims C124-C126 about whether systemic acidosis explains the airway phenotype. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on transporter saturation kinetics from cited work. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, specifically questioning whether the transporter is saturated at 5 mM HCO3- and requesting experimental verification rather than relying on citation.

OpenEval evaluates C71-C75, C106 about mouse phenotype and localization. Peer reviewers evaluate C106-C109 about species differences in cellular localization. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers suggested future experiments with cell-specific knockouts but accepted the localization findings.

Both evaluate claims C107-C109 (among others) about species differences in airway cell types. Both find SUPPORTED. The context about CFTR and pendrin expression in Club cells versus ciliated cells in different species was accepted as accurately cited background information.

OpenEval evaluates claims C96, C101 about CFTR-SLC4A4 functional coupling and finds SUPPORTED based on localization correlation and cited pancreatic duct studies, though notes direct demonstration in airways would strengthen conclusions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates claim C23 about controversial ASL pH findings in CF and rates UNCERTAIN due to conflicting reports in the literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates claims C129-C133 about why lung defects are not reported in human SLC4A4 patients and rates UNCERTAIN, noting explanations are speculative and could reflect ascertainment bias. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates claims C136-C141 about isoform-specific knockouts and genetic background effects and finds SUPPORTED by authors' observations and cited work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C1-C7 about CF pathophysiology and finds SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C17-C22 about CF pathophysiology and finds SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C24-C27 about therapeutic relevance and finds SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C28-C30 identifying the knowledge gap and finds SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C90-C91, C94 and finds SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C97-C100 about functional coupling in pancreatic ducts and finds SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C112-C115 about limitations of previous work and finds SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates claims C119-C123 about consequences of impaired bicarbonate secretion and finds SUPPORTED by multiple citations. Peer reviewers evaluated C123 in context of R11 concerns about confounders. No direct peer evaluation of C119-C122 found.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C127-C128 about systemic Slc4a4-/- phenotype and finds SUPPORTED by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates claims C102-C103 about potential compensation mechanisms and rates UNCERTAIN, noting C103 is speculative without direct evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates claims C134-C135 about potential compensation in humans and rates UNCERTAIN, noting C135 is speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
